design:
TARGET REPO: meridianlabs-ai/inspect_swe (mapping code lives in src/inspect_swe/_claude_code/_events/; inspect_scout wraps it; fixture tests live in inspect_scout, so a PR likely touches both).

DRAFT ISSUE (for Luke to review, edit and file himself):

Title: Claude Code transcript import: record user interrupts and tool-use rejections as events

## Feature request

**Problem.** `_claude_code/_events` (used by inspect_scout's `claude_code()` source) records nothing for the human's actions in a session other than prompt text:

- Typed prompts become `ChatMessageUser` with no `source` (extraction.py L37-80, `extract_user_message`) and appear only inside a later `ModelEvent`'s input. `isMeta`/`userType` are not read, so typed prompts and injected text look the same.
- Interrupt markers ("[Request interrupted by user]") are kept as ordinary user text. No `InterruptEvent` is emitted.
- A rejected tool call becomes `ToolCallError(type="unknown")`, the same as any other tool failure (events.py L243-256). Feedback the user gave with the denial stays inside the error string.

/clear and compaction are already handled (`split_on_clear`, `CompactionEvent`).

**Why.** Analysing human-in-the-loop sessions needs to find where the person stepped in. Today that means pattern-matching message text against strings Claude Code may change.

**Proposal** (existing types only):
1. Rejection -> `ApprovalEvent(call=<ToolCall>, approver="human", decision="reject", explanation=<feedback or None>)` before the `ToolEvent`, with `ToolEvent.error.type="approval"`.
2. Interrupt -> `InterruptEvent(source="user_cancel", interrupted="tool_call" | "generate", interrupted_tool_call_id=...)`.
3. Typed prompts -> `ChatMessageUser(source=...)` for non-meta user entries.

Detection strings in one function, with fixture tests; unknown shapes fall back to current behaviour.

**Questions.**
- Is `ApprovalEvent` right for a rejection with no approval policy? Approvals aren't in the transcript, so only rejections would appear.
- Should `approver` be "human", with the person in `metadata["decided_by"]` as in inspect_ai#6520?
- Should typed prompts use `source="input"` or `"operator"`, or should they get an event of their own?
- Which repo should own this: here, or in inspect_scout, where the fixtures live?

I can implement this with fixture transcripts (interrupt, deny, deny with feedback) if accepted.

*Drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code); I've reviewed it and checked the references against main.*
acceptance_criteria: Luke has reviewed and filed the issue; its URL is saved with bd remember.
notes: Source verified 2026-11-16 at inspect_swe c50ce3c, inspect_scout bf32fa3, inspect_ai 8c2e11f. Related: inspect_swe#66 (operator intervention through the bridge, the live counterpart), inspect_ai#6520 (decided_by metadata convention), inspect_scout#629, inspect_ai PRs #6487 and #6296 (merged, live path). Rules: inspect_swe has no issue-first text but PR titles must be Conventional Commits and an agent-co-authored PR needs an '### Agent review' section; inspect_scout/inspect_ai need an 'accepted' issue before code. LOCAL EVIDENCE from 277 transcripts on this machine (Claude Code 2.1.274 era): '[Request interrupted by user]' 111 and '[Request interrupted by user for tool use]' 24, almost all as plain text blocks with no toolUseResult; rejections appear as tool_result blocks with is_error true and a STRING toolUseResult ('User rejected tool use' x30, 'Error: The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use.' x8); denial feedback follows 'the user said:'. userType was 'external' on all 57,221 user entries, so userType does NOT separate typed prompts from injected text; isMeta was true on 1,007. Draft item 3 was adjusted accordingly. Not verified: whether approvals are recorded at all; marker stability across Claude Code versions. Luke must review the draft and file it; nothing has been posted.

title: Telemetry receiver: capture Claude Code's OpenTelemetry export
description: Goodall's own standard-library receiver for Claude Code's OTLP http/json export (decision 2026-11-16; the official Collector is optional, not a dependency). Listens on 127.0.0.1 only, accepts POSTs to /v1/logs, /v1/metrics and /v1/traces, and appends each request body verbatim as one line to a per-signal JSON Lines file under the log directory, flushed per write. Started with a work block and stopped at its end; the work-block record states whether telemetry was captured. Because Claude Code silently drops telemetry when nothing is listening, the hook path checks the receiver is up and doctor reports it. Onboarding sets the Claude Code telemetry environment (enable flag, exporters, http/json protocol, endpoint, traces beta flag). Open questions to settle when building: whether prompt, response and tool-detail content flags are on by default (transcripts already hold content; telemetry carries email and account ids on every record either way); how the receiver process is supervised across sleep and crashes. Evidence and field lists: bd memories SPIKE goodall-fs9.2.
acceptance_criteria: Start from a failing outside-in test: a fake Claude Code POST to the receiver results in one verbatim line in the right file. A real work block yields logs, metrics and traces files whose session.id matches the transcript filename; killing the receiver mid-session loses no already-acknowledged line; a work block with the receiver down still captures transcripts and records telemetry as missing; capture code imports only the standard library.

title: goodall hook: prompt gate and heartbeat
description: Entry point Claude Code hooks call. UserPromptSubmit refuses the prompt with the fix ('goodall session start') when no work block is active; every event records a heartbeat and links the Claude session id to the work block. Imports standard library only.
acceptance_criteria: A test asserts the hook module imports nothing third-party; gate refusal and pass-through both tested from recorded hook input; measured start-up time noted.
notes: Design inputs from spike fs9.1: gate via UserPromptSubmit exit 2 + stderr reason or JSON {decision:block}; claude -p exits 0 on refusal, so callers cannot use the exit code; refused prompt text still lands in the transcript (queue-operation and system entries); ~30ms overhead for a stdlib python hook; heartbeat on PostToolUse.

title: Incremental transcript sync
description: Copy Claude Code transcripts verbatim into the log directory in Claude Code's own layout (including subagent files) after each response via an async Stop hook, with SessionEnd as a top-up and a sweep on the next session start or any goodall command. Never overwrite a copy when the source has shrunk; keep both.
acceptance_criteria: Killing a session mid-turn loses nothing after the next sweep; Scout's claude_code importer reads the copied directory unchanged; shrink case tested.
notes: Design inputs from spike fs9.1: trigger incremental copy on PostToolUse (per tool call) as well as Stop (once per run) and SessionEnd; a copy at PostToolUse is one step behind by nature; async hooks are SIGTERMed at process exit so the copy must be fast and atomic (write temp then rename); SIGKILL fires no hooks, so the sweep on next start is the only guarantee; copy the <session_id>/subagents/ folder including .meta.json and .prefix.json.
